source_of_truth: Two independent sources, both verified by reading the pinned code: (1) the Juice Shop project's own in-source challenge markers — lines tagged '// vuln-code-snippet vuln-line <challenge>' mark the vulnerable lines the project itself documents; (2) direct code reading of endpoints whose flaws are visible without running the app (SSRF fetch, path-join sendFile, hardcoded RSA private key). Juice Shop's full vulnerability list is much larger than these labels; recall is therefore measured only against the labeled subset, and findings in unlabeled files are reported but not scored.

routes/search.ts.note: vuln-line marker: unionSqlInjectionChallenge — template literal into sequelize.query.

routes/login.ts.note: vuln-line marker: loginAdminChallenge et al. — req.body.email interpolated into sequelize.query.

routes/updateProductReviews.ts.note: vuln-line marker: noSqlReviewsChallenge — req.body.id used as a Mongo update filter.

frontend/src/app/search-result/search-re.note: vuln-line marker: restfulXssChallenge/localXssChallenge — bypassSecurityTrustHtml on product description and query param.

routes/profileImageUrlUpload.ts.note: inspection: fetch(req.body.imageUrl) with no allowlist (the code even tracks its own abuse).

routes/fileServer.ts.note: inspection: res.sendFile(path.resolve('ftp/', params.file)) — directory escape gated only by a '/'-in-name check and a null-byte filter that the project documents as bypassable.

routes/keyServer.ts.note: inspection: res.sendFile(path.resolve('encryptionkeys/', params.file)) with the same weak gate — serves the JWT signing keys.

routes/logfileServer.ts.note: inspection: res.sendFile(path.resolve('logs/', params.file)) with the same weak gate.

lib/insecurity.ts.note: inspection: RSA private key as a string literal in source — the JWT signing key.
